purpose: Prove capture emits the four attributes the deterministic field classifier reads - autocomplete, inputmode, placeholder and id - so classify() rung 1 (the app's OWN W3C declaration of what a field is for) can fire on a live crawl instead of being unreachable code.
targeted_defect: BUG-CAPTURE-ATTRS: describe() (inventory_js.py:561-631) emits none of autocomplete/inputmode/placeholder/id, and build_control_record() (inventory.py:584-646) does not carry them either. field_signature.compute() reads all four (field_signature.py:157-164,190) and field_semantics.classify() weights autocomplete FIRST at confidence 0.98 (field_semantics.py:190-195). With capture silent, rung 1 can never fire on a crawled control, the placeholder/id token fallbacks for nameless fields are dead, and every field falls through to the weakest name-token rung.

expect_controls.why: With no label/aria/title the placeholder is the ONLY name rung left, so the walker already reads the attribute - it simply never emits it as a field of its own.
No name of any kind. Its semantics live entirely in the id, which is exactly why id must be captured.

describes_correct_behaviour.why: The label tokens ('Field A7') classify to nothing. Only the declared autocomplete can name this field.
Multi-token autocomplete must survive capture intact - classify() scans the tokens in reverse and needs them all.
autocomplete/inputmode are case-insensitive enumerated keywords, normalised at capture the same way role and aria-haspopup already are. placeholder is human text and is preserved verbatim.
ABSENT must capture as empty string, never null and never invented.
PRESENT-BUT-EMPTY must be indistinguishable from absent.
Captured honestly, but classify() excludes on/off so rung 1 must NOT fire on it. Asserted in test_capture_contract.py.
